propositions: 53 production C901 diagnostics exist above complexity 15 in src/rebar, blocking the gate if raw Ruff exit code 1 is treated as failure; a wrapper baseline mechanism is needed to accept bounded legacy debt while rejecting new or increased complexity.

The wrapper accepts Ruff return codes 0 and 1 as normal diagnostic-bearing operation after validating C901 JSON; return code 2+ is a scanner failure; it compares current findings against a committed baseline using AST-qualified symbol keys and exits zero only when all findings are at or below recorded ceilings.
The --update-stale guarded maintenance mode can lower or remove stale debt through atomic writes but refuses to write when new or increased debt exists, preventing silent absorption of regressions.

Baseline JSON schema requires schema_version 1, sorted ceiling keys in form path::qualified-symbol with integers > 15, rejection of duplicates and unknown fields, and four mutually exclusive counters (active, new, increased, stale) derived from comparison logic.

Symbol identity is derived from Python AST FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef nodes only; class/function ancestry disambiguates equal leaf names; lambdas and overloads must not create ambiguous or duplicate qualified keys; normalization fails rather than overwriting on collision.

The wrapper is wired into make lint alongside existing src/tests linting, with baseline check command documented in maintenance runbook using threshold 15 and src/rebar scope; no inline or per-file C901 ignores are permitted.
